svg.title: A section of the city's fortified stone wall in winter: two mortared ashlar faces meeting at a salient angle, the near face lit in the limestone base tone and the returning face in its shade tone, BOTH BATTERED so the wall leans back as it rises and stands wider at the foot than at the head - the corner runs from a foot at x 252 to a head at x 230, twenty-two pixels inboard over a three hundred and forty-eight pixel rise, and the returning face's outer edge leans the opposite way by the same amount, so the whole mass splays toward the ground the way a rampart does and not the way a garden wall does. A plain flat coping runs unbroken round the corner and projects over both faces with a shadow line under it, snow lies along its head, corner quoins step down the angle, and the courses and the staggered vertical joints lean WITH the batter. NO CRENELLATION, no battlements, no merlons, no arrow slits, no tower, no turret, no gate, no cannon: the wall in the reference has a plain coping and none of those. No lettering, no plaque, no flag, no figure. No brick - that ramp belongs to the Chateau and is forbidden here. Drawn from assets/refs/quebec-city/quebec-ramparts-snow.jpg, a geometry and arrangement reference only; every colour is from palette.json. See assets/refs/references.json, subject city-wall. POI hero, present at every visual tier.
